newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Guinea Bissau to join West Africa's CFA franc zone.
newsitem.headline: Guinea Bissau to join West Africa's CFA franc zone.

text.p: Portuguese-speaking Guinea Bissau is to join West Africa's CFA franc zone, with May 2 the target date for entry, the region's Central Bank said in a statement on Tuesday.
The exchange rate for its peso currency on entry would be 65 to one French-backed CFA franc, the statement added.
The statement said the heads of state of the seven members of the West African Monetary Union (UMOA), France and the International Monetary Fund had all agreed to the principle of the move.

"To take account of the legal and technical constraints linked to this membership, the parties agreed to aim for May 2 1997 for the start of the operations to change the monetary symbols," the Dakar-based Central Bank (BCEAO) added.
Guinea Bissau, borders Senegal, which is a member of the zone, and Guinea, which is not. It became independent in 1974.
The other members of the zone, all former French colonies, are Benin, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger and Togo.
